newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ten killed, 49 injured in Colombian bomb blast.
newsitem.headline: Ten killed, 49 injured in Colombian bomb blast.

text.p: At least 10 people were killed and more than 45 injured on Thursday when a powerful bomb blast tore through a town in Colombia's notoriously violent northwest banana-growing region of Uraba, authorities said.

The death toll from the morning blast was initially set at seven, but police and municipal officials in the bloodied town of Apartado raised it to 10 after rescue workers pulled the bodies of two men and a woman from the rubble of a hotel that was leveled by the explosion.

The town's mayor, Omar Largo Penilla, told national radio that at least one other person was missing in the gutted remains of the four-story El Pescador Hotel and that the number of fatalities was likely to climb to at least 11.
The dead included a 3-year-old child and a policeman, and Largo said some 49 people were injured.
A regional military commander, Gen. Ivan Ramirez, blamed the bombing on leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels.

Police sources told Reuters the bomb -- which exploded in the back of a pickup truck at about 8:50 a.m. local time (1350 GMT) -- was believed to have been comprised of up to 220 pounds (100 kg) of dynamite.
Eight other nearby buildings, including the town's police headquarters, suffered serious structural damage and Largo said damages had been estimated at more than $1.5 million.

At least six guerrillas were killed in a firefight with the military on Sunday in Uraba, and Ramirez said the truck bomb was meant to avenge both the deaths and the army's recent dismantling of several rebel encampments in Uraba.

The vehicle in which the bomb exploded had been rented by the municipality of Apartado for use as a garbage truck, according to Ramirez. He said it was hijacked by suspected guerrillas about 7 a.m., laden with the dynamite and parked along the town's main street, about 65 feet (20 meters) from the police station.
Deputy National Police chief Gen. Luis Ernesto Gilibert told Reuters police were unable to confirm that the bomb had been set by guerrillas.
"It's too soon for us to attribute responsibility," he said.

He did not elaborate, but gunmen of the left and right have killed with impunity throughout Uraba for more than a decade. Guerrillas and right-wing paramilitary groups based in the impoverished region, on the Caribbean coast near Colombia's border with Panama, have long been known to control lucrative arms and drug smuggling routes.

In violence elsewhere in Colombia, authorities said two policemen were killed and four others wounded in an overnight attack by about 200 FARC rebels on the small town of Labranzagrande in the Cordillera Oriental mountains of central Boyaca province.

The town's 14-strong police force held off the rebels, who launched their attack around midnight, until army reinforcements forced them to retreat into the surrounding mountains shortly after dawn, police said.
The police headquarters was destroyed and a cook working inside was wounded in the fighting after she took up a rifle to back the police.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, was founded as a Marxist-led, pro-Soviet group in 1964.
